appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: mid-green leaves; white umbels.

appearance.organs.basal.note: Its basal leaves as its stem leaves (Abrams 1951: ternate, the leaflets broad and lobed), on longer petioles, by eye.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.leaflets.note: How PlantGen draws a divided leaf, a choice of the model's (spec rework P4): the leaf characters set a compound card's pattern, its leaflets or pinnae, the leaflets on each pinna, and whether its segments run together. A pinnate leaf's count says how it ends (odd-pinnate odd, even-pinnate even), so a flora's range is drawn as the nearest count of the right kind.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its compound umbel drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c): its kind from the carrot family's inflorescence and its rays from its own, by the rules at the flowering plants; about 20 flowers in each umbellet (Illinois Wildflowers gives 8 to 30; no flora gives a count), each about 6 mm across with five white notched petals, on pedicels 1 to 2 cm long (Jepson: 8 to 20 mm), the umbel about 25 cm across (the Flora of North America: 15 to 30 cm). From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. The enlarged outer flowers are not drawn. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five white notched petals with no sepals (by hand: sepals obsolete, Abrams's Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States, 1951, read in full) on the inferior ovary, five stamens and a pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Apiaceae by the rules at the flowering plants.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a giant herb with hollow stems, huge maple-like leaves of three lobed leaflets and broad, flat umbrellas of white flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.basal_length.note: How PlantGen's herb program sizes a herb's leaves from a flora's leaf lengths, a choice of the model's (spec rework E1 and E3): its longest stem and basal leaves as long as the longest leaf the flora gives, its lowest and topmost stem leaves shorter by the shortest's share of it, the card's petiole part of the length. Homed at the campanulids, where it holds for the daisy and carrot families and changes no other built-in species.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): the sexual system its taxa state most often decides; a species whose taxa state dioecy no more often than another system bears both sexes on every plant until it states its own.

generator.params.leaf_base.note: How PlantGen's herb program sizes a herb's leaves from a flora's leaf lengths, a choice of the model's (spec rework E1 and E3): its longest stem and basal leaves as long as the longest leaf the flora gives, its lowest and topmost stem leaves shorter by the shortest's share of it, the card's petiole part of the length. Homed at the campanulids, where it holds for the daisy and carrot families and changes no other built-in species.

generator.params.leaves_per_node.note: What the words mean, as accounts of phyllotaxis such as Okabe and colleagues' use them: a spiral or two-ranked shoot bears one leaf at a node, a decussate one a pair and a whorled one three or more. A spiral turns about the golden angle (137.5 degrees) from node to node and two ranks half a turn; pairs and whorls alternate, each standing over the gaps of the one below, half the gap between its own leaves round (90 degrees for pairs). Three ranks turn a third of a turn, as their name says.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.
